title: MCX Q1 Profit Drops 22% Sequentially as Revenue Slides From Record Quarter
excerpt: India's dominant commodity exchange posted Rs 413 crore in net profit on Rs 702 crore revenue in Q1 FY27, marking a sharp pullback from Q4 FY26's all-time highs, though year-on-year growth remains robust.
body:
• MCX consolidated net profit fell 22% quarter-on-quarter to Rs 413 crore in Q1 FY27, down from Rs 530 crore in Q4 FY26, while revenue declined 21% sequentially to Rs 702 crore.
  • EBITDA dropped 25.8% QoQ to Rs 494 crore with margins contracting 450 basis points to 70.4%, reflecting a step-down from Q4 FY26's exceptional 74.9%.
  • Year-on-year, the picture remains strong: revenue nearly doubled from Rs 373 crore, while profit more than doubled from Rs 203 crore reported in Q1 FY26.
  • MCX retains over 98% market share in commodity futures and ranks as the world's largest commodity options exchange by contract volume.

Multi Commodity Exchange of India reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 413 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, a 22% decline from the Rs 530 crore posted in the preceding January-March quarter, according to NDTV Profit. Revenue from operations fell 21% sequentially to Rs 702 crore from Q4 FY26's Rs 889 crore.

The results mark a clear step-down from what was a record-breaking Q4 FY26 for India's dominant commodity derivatives exchange. In that quarter, MCX had reported its highest-ever revenue and profit, driven by a surge in bullion trading and expanded options volumes.

Margins Contract From Peak Levels

EBITDA for the quarter fell 25.8% sequentially to Rs 494 crore, with the EBITDA margin compressing 450 basis points to 70.4% from 74.9% in Q4 FY26. While this represents a notable pullback, the margin level remains well above the 64.7% MCX had posted in Q1 FY26 and the 63% full-year average for FY25.

MCX peer BSE, by contrast, reported a sequential improvement in Q1 FY27, with net profit rising 9.7% to Rs 874 crore on flat revenue of Rs 1,566 crore, according to NDTV Profit.

Year-on-Year Growth Remains Robust

Viewed against the year-ago quarter, MCX's Q1 FY27 performance tells a different story. Revenue nearly doubled from the Rs 373 crore reported in Q1 FY26, while net profit more than doubled from Rs 203 crore. The year-on-year trajectory reflects the exchange's strong underlying momentum, buoyed by rapid growth in options trading volumes and rising participation across bullion and energy segments.

"We began this financial year on a positive note, demonstrating resilience, adaptability, and strategic focus amid a continuously evolving market environment."

— Praveena Rai, Managing Director & CEO, MCX (Q1 FY26 earnings)

During FY26, MCX's average daily turnover in futures and options surged 145% year-on-year to Rs 5.4 lakh crore. The exchange also climbed to become the world's largest commodity options exchange and the fourth-largest commodity exchange globally, according to FIA data for 2025, up from sixth in 2024.

Dominant Market Position Intact

MCX continues to command over 98% market share in commodity futures turnover in India. The exchange ended FY26 with 20.9 lakh traded clients in futures and options, up from 13 lakh in FY25. Revenue is increasingly diversified, with futures contributing Rs 693 crore and options Rs 1,398 crore in FY26, both registering triple-digit year-on-year growth.

New product launches in FY26, including Electricity Futures, BULLDEX Options, and monthly Gold and Silver options contracts, have broadened MCX's product suite. The exchange has also launched a "Price in India: Hedge in India" initiative aimed at deepening hedging participation, particularly among MSMEs and physical market players.

What's Next

Management had guided during the FY26 results that FY27 would be another strong year, though cyclicality could affect quarterly results — a caution the Q1 numbers appear to validate. The exchange's board had also recommended a final dividend of Rs 8 per share for FY26, pending shareholder approval at the annual general meeting.

For investors, the sequential decline may test near-term sentiment. MCX shares have gained nearly 68% over the past year, according to ScanX data, but the stock has slipped 4.8% in the last month. The key question is whether the trading volume surge that powered FY26's record performance can sustain through FY27, or if the Q1 pullback signals a broader normalization.
nri_angle: MCX's dominant position in India's commodity derivatives market makes it a closely watched stock among NRI investors with exposure to Indian financial infrastructure plays.
